transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 min
Attendees: Sam Park (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CSM), Jonas Meyer (Solutions Eng), Maya Chen (CTO - Orion), Raj Patel (Head of MLOps), Noah Brown (VP Product), Elena Ruiz (SRE Lead)

Optional summary:
- Goal: monthly health check: usage patterns, cost anomalies, reliability incidents, roadmap alignment and pilot next steps.
- Big items: two latency incidents last week (traffic spike), discussion of Dedicated bursts vs hosted fallback, and next steps for a 2-week pilot bench.

Topics: usage deltas, cost drivers, autoscale behavior, cache warming, SSO/KMS questions, pilot scope, SOC2 docs.

[00:00] Sam: hey everyone, thanks for making time, happy to see familiar faces. quick roll call?
[00:12] Maya: Maya here.
[00:14] Raj: Raj.
[00:15] Noah: Noah, hi.
[00:16] Elena: Elena on my side.
[00:18] Sam: great. from Redwood we have Lena, Priya and Jonas listed — thanks. we'll keep this to 45 mins and leave 7 for q&a.
[00:30] Lena: quick agenda: run through last 30 days of usage, surface the two latency blips, talk about Dedicated vs Hosted economics, then proposed pilot/bench plan.
[00:44] Raj: that works. wanted to flag we had two production slowdown windows last tuesday morning and again friday afternoon, both during batch promotions.
[00:55] Sam: yeah saw alerts, can you help us with timelines? approximate windows and error types?
[01:05] Raj: first was 09:12–09:27 UTC, spike in p95 from 140ms to 620ms, some 429s at 09:14–09:16. second was 15:05–15:22, similar p95 bump and a few OOMs reported by the orchestrator.
[01:25] Lena: thanks. did you have any retries or client-side batching changes in those windows?
[01:33] Raj: we rolled a release at 08:50 that increased concurrency per pod, so probably correlated. also we tweaked prefix caching for the recommender endpoint.
[01:42] Lena: got it — so two levers: traffic-concurrency change and cache behavior. we often see kv cache warm-up causing 1st-request latency. sometimes transcripts say KV cash in our logs — small thing but it confuses ops.
[01:56] Noah: small thing but yeah, logs show weirdness. what's Redwood's typical mitigation?
[02:03] Sam: a few: autoscale policy changes, pre-warming model instances (we can do scheduled warm pools), and for high-p95 workloads we recommend Dedicated with burst enabled so you have baseline qps and a burst buffer.
[02:16] Maya: curious on cost delta. our finance team is worried Dedicated + burst could blow monthly spend.
[02:23] Sam: totally reasonable. we'll send a cost playbook — it shows committed baseline pricing + per-burst units. for many customers the unit cost for steady traffic is 30–40% lower on Dedicated when you commit. bursts are metered differently but still usually cheaper than high peak in hosted because batching and concurrency are optimized.
[02:43] Raj: what about graceful degradation? if burst pool exhausted will Redwood route to hosted fallback?
[02:50] Jonas: yes, policy-based routing can failover to compatible hosted variants. note that model quantization or variant mismatch can change output slightly, so we recommend canary to verify quality.
[03:04] Elena: we care about deterministic output for our recommender. any model variant mismatch could break downstream product heuristics.
[03:12] Lena: understood — we can configure rollout policy: strict version pin for recommender route, non-strict for experiments. Also we can do A/B with fallback only for non-critical endpoints.
[03:26] Noah: can you share an example policy?
[03:29] Lena: yes, I'll attach a sample routing policy after call.
[03:32] Sam: switching to costs: Lena, can you summarize cost drivers we saw for Orion last month?
[03:38] Lena: sure — pull from Oct usage: tokens up 18% due to marketing campaign, 62% of tokens came from the recommender endpoint, and 75% of request tail was short inference (<64 tokens) but high qps. Small model runs with high qps often get hit by per-request overhead — batching helps but latency SLOs limited batching window. Also we saw 40% of requests had cold KV cache misses first token.
[04:05] Raj: odd — our cache TTLs are 2 hours, should be warm. maybe the prefix keys changed after the launch?
[04:10] Elena: there were schema changes to the prefix key format in the release.
[04:14] Lena: that explains it. when keys change you lose cache hit rate, which increases per-token compute and cost.
[04:20] Maya: can Redwood help identify cache miss patterns?
[04:23] Lena: yes — we can run a cache-hit analysis and surface hot keys. we'll need a week of traces (sampled).
[04:30] Raj: we can export that. action: I'll pull a 7-day request trace with headers and sample prompts.
[04:36] Sam: perfect. next, reliability incidents: do you have SLOs defined?
[04:40] Elena: target 99.9% p99 under normal load, p95 under 200ms for recommender. we missed p99 once during the spike.
[04:49] Sam: okay, we can map those to Redwood monitors and set alert thresholds. we also offer tracing hooks to correlate model latency with infra metrics.
[04:58] Noah: on security/compliance — we got security questions from procurement: SOC2, SAML/SSO integration, audit logs, KMS. any new docs?
[05:10] Priya: yes, I'll attach SOC2 Type II and ISO pack after this. we also have a short doc on SSO and SCIM provisioning. for KMS workflows, our Private deployment supports customer-managed keys (HSM or cloud KMS).
[05:25] Maya: for us the requirement is keys held in our AWS KMS and audit logs stored for 1 year.
[05:30] Priya: that's supported on Redwood Private. for hosted we can do envelope encryption with customer KMS in some cases; I'll confirm details.
[05:39] Raj: could you restate the difference between Private and Dedicated for us? we want clear guidance.
[05:45] Sam: short version: Dedicated is Redwood-managed infra dedicated to you (pooled GPUs you commit to) — good for throughput predictability and lower per-unit cost. Private is customer network (VPC) or on-prem control plane option with customer-managed KMS, stricter network isolation and longer procurement.
[06:03] Maya: procurement timeline?
[06:05] Sam: Dedicated pilot we can start in 2 weeks once PO signed; Private typically 6–8 weeks for network setup and security review.
[06:13] Noah: any benchmarks we can use for sizing?
[06:15] Lena: yes — we ran local benches for your workload on similar models: 2.7B with prompt length 128, batch size 8, A100 avg token latency ~40ms; T4 equivalent ~95–120ms with optimized kernels. 13B numbers increase accordingly. I'll upload the CSV and perf notes.
[06:34] Raj: those A100 numbers look promising. are they with quantization?
[06:38] Lena: the A100 run was fp16; T4 was int8 quant with some accuracy checks. quantization can alter outputs slightly; we can run a quality regression on your golden prompts.
[06:48] Maya: we need to validate output parity before commit.
[06:50] Jonas: propose: 2-week bench where Redwood runs full perf and quality regression on your golden set and returns a report. pilot includes: Dedicated baseline sizing, burst policy, and failover plan.
[07:03] Noah: cost of the bench?
[07:05] Sam: we typically absorb initial bench for strategic pilots; if long extended runs or heavy GPU time, there may be a nominal engineering fee. we'll outline that.
[07:14] Maya: good. can you show what alerts would look like?
[07:17] Lena: short demo — pulling up the console (screen share) — bear with me if transcription garbles some names.
[07:24] [screen share noise]
[07:32] Lena: here is the per-route latency view, token breakdown by user token vs system prompt, and cost burn on a per-model basis. see that spike on Oct 12? that's the marketing campaign. we can add route-level SLOs and set runbook links.
[07:50] Elena: that runbook link — can it post to our PagerDuty?
[07:53] Lena: yes, we have webhook integrations for PagerDuty and Datadog — we can configure on a per-route basis.
[07:59] Raj: two more technical questions: 1) how does KV cache work across Dedicated nodes? and 2) what happens to cached state on auto-scale down?
[08:08] Lena: KV cache is local to the serving node; we also do a shared prefix cache for hot keys. on scale down we flush local caches unless you enable sticky sessions or a shared cache layer. for strictly deterministic workloads we recommend sticky sessions plus cache replication or using tokenized prompts to reduce variability.
[08:25] Raj: sticky sessions sound risky for long tail scaling. any best practices?
[08:29] Lena: keep prefix keys stable, increase cache TTL for hot keys, and use pre-warming for high-peak windows. also route critical traffic to Dedicated baseline to avoid eviction.
[08:42] Maya: will Redwood provide tooling to repro the blips locally?
[08:46] Jonas: yes, we'll use a replay harness — if you provide request traces we can replay and reproduce the incident in our staging cluster. it's helpful to include timing and concurrency metadata.
[08:58] Raj: noted.
[09:00] Noah: quick question on billing visibility — can we get token-level reports by route daily?
[09:06] Sam: yes, per-route token+cost export available daily with CSV or JSON. we'll attach a sample export.
[09:12] Maya: let's get that for Oct 10–17 period to see the campaign spike.
[09:16] Sam: noted.
[09:18] Priya: returning to compliance — I'll post SOC2, SAML guide, and KMS notes to the CRM deal after call.
[09:24] Maya: thanks. earlier you mentioned fallback to hosted variants — how are we guaranteed no regressions?
[09:31] Lena: we allow pinned model versions and a canary rollout where a small % of traffic goes to fallback and outputs are validated via a scoring harness. if quality falls below threshold we auto-failback.
[09:44] Elena: does that scoring harness support custom metrics? we use a business metric that flags a mismatch in top-5 items.
[09:51] Lena: yes you can plug in custom comparators and thresholds.
[09:55] Raj: on pilot scope: what's minimum commit for Dedicated to make it worthwhile?
[09:59] Sam: depends on qps and concurrency. for your peak patterns (estimated steady qps ~450 during day) we'd recommend a baseline of 6 GPUs with burst up to 10 for traffic peaks — will share sizing. that usually needs a monthly commit to show meaningful unit cost reductions.
[10:17] Noah: can we do monthly commit with a short-term trial?
[10:20] Sam: yes — pilot contract with a month commit plus 2-week bench.
[10:24] Maya: procurement will want pricing matrix and worst-case spend.
[10:28] Sam: we'll include an 'expected vs worst-case' spend sheet and show how burst metering caps work.
[10:35] Raj: one security nuance: we rotate keys nightly; will that affect cache or sessions?
[10:40] Lena: if keys rotate and are bound to session encryption, yes you may see transient failures unless rotation is orchestrated with grace period. recommend rotation window overlap for KMS.
[10:50] Elena: we can do that.
[10:52] Sam: quick recap of items we committed to: 1) provide Dedicated pricing + burst playbook; 2) Lena will upload bench results and perf CSV; 3) Raj to supply 7-day trace; 4) Priya to push SOC2 & open pilot in CRM; 5) schedule technical deep dive w/ SREs week of Oct 25.
[11:12] Noah: sounds good — what's the timeline for the bench report?
[11:15] Lena: 3 business days after we receive traces and golden prompts, so target Oct 21.
[11:21] Sam: I'll send the pricing sheet by EOD Oct 19.
[11:25] Priya: I'll create the pilot deal in CRM and attach SOC2 and SSO docs (deal id ORN-2027-4821).
[11:33] Maya: one last ask — can Redwood run a quick smoke test at ramp time to validate end-to-end?
[11:39] Jonas: yes we'll coordinate and run a smoke with your SREs.
[11:42] Elena: ok please include networking checklist for dedicated. we've had surprises before.
[11:46] Sam: will do.
[11:47] [brief hold / background noise]
[11:55] Noah: ok thanks all. any final Qs?
[11:59] Maya: no, thanks — excited to get the bench started.
[12:03] Sam: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with notes and attach artifacts (pricing sheet, bench CSV, SOC2 link). meeting adjourned.
